questions.q: At a high level, when does an LOD expression compute compared to a table calculation?
options: An LOD expression computes at query time, alongside the data source query; a table calculation computes after the query returns, on the already-aggregated result set
Both compute at exactly the same time, in the same place
A table calculation always computes before an LOD expression, regardless of type
An LOD expression only computes when the workbook is published to Tableau Server
questions.explain: LOD expressions run as part of the query sent to the data source. Table calculations run afterward, working only with the aggregated values already in the view.

questions.q: Why can't an LOD expression compute a running total or a rank the way a table calculation can?
options: LOD expressions have no concept of row position or order within the visible table — they only know dimensions and aggregations
LOD expressions are slower than table calculations, so Tableau blocks this use case
Running totals and ranks require a live database connection, which LOD expressions can't use
This isn't true — LOD expressions can compute running totals just as easily
questions.explain: Running totals, rank, and moving averages all depend on a row's position relative to others in the current table layout — something only a table calculation's addressing/partitioning can express.

questions.q: Why can a FIXED LOD expression reference a dimension that isn't anywhere on the current view, while a table calculation cannot?
options: LOD expressions compute against the underlying data source before aggregation, reaching detail the view's result set doesn't even contain; table calculations only work with what's already in the view's result set
Table calculations can also do this — there's no real restriction
FIXED LOD expressions are actually a special kind of table calculation
This is only true for INCLUDE and EXCLUDE, not FIXED
questions.explain: LOD expressions run at query time against the full data source, so they can reach dimensions never placed on the view. Table calculations only ever see the aggregated rows already returned to the view.

questions.q: You need a percent-of-total calculation that changes correctly as a user applies different filters and reference the CURRENTLY VISIBLE rows in the table. What should you use?
options: A table calculation (percent of total, computed using the relevant field)
A FIXED LOD expression with an empty scope
An EXCLUDE LOD expression
A context filter with no calculation at all
questions.explain: Percent of the currently visible rows is exactly what a table calculation is for — it recalculates based on whatever's actually in the table after filtering, unlike a FIXED expression which is designed to stay independent of the view.

questions.q: According to this lesson's decision table, what should you use for 'a number independent of the current view,' like customer lifetime value?
options: FIXED LOD
A table calculation with Compute Using set to Table (Across)
EXCLUDE LOD
A context filter
questions.explain: FIXED is designed precisely for values that should stay constant regardless of how the view is sliced — the opposite of what a table calculation, which depends on the visible table, is built for.
